claims.text: The driver's explanation for stopping roughly 200 metres short of the pin - that 'the last stretch is a bus lane' - is an assertion of an external traffic cause, and there is no artifact behind it. The traffic_advisory for this trip, EV-ADVIS-00536-01, is MISSING from the bundle, carries weight_multiplier 0.0 and fired the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and the rider discloses that impairment as POL-GEN-02(1) requires. Nothing on file names a road, expressway segment or junction that the optimal route traverses for this window, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run at all. Under POL-RD-13 the driver's assertion is tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else, and under POL-RD-08 an uncited assertion of bad traffic carries no weight and is discarded. The driver's excuse therefore explains nothing, exonerates nothing and reduces no excess.

Nor can the driver fall back on a rider-requested detour or stop. The chat_log for this trip, EV-CHAT-00536, is COMPLETE and records zero messages - first_message_at and last_message_at are both null and message_count is 0 - so there is no rider instruction that could exonerate any part of the route under POL-RD-04, and the driver's 'I told them where to go' exists only as an unsworn statement with no recorded message behind it. Both exculpatory routes open to the driver, POL-RD-03 and POL-RD-04, are closed on this record.

The substance of the rider's complaint is confirmed by the platform's own record, not merely by her account: the trip_record's dropoff is labelled 'Marina Coastal Dr, 210 m short of the pier', so the recorded completion point is not the destination the rider pinned, and the driver's own statement concedes the same 200 metre gap. That dropoff-point discrepancy is what POL-RD-05 governs, but the record carries no dropoff_amended_at and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so the clause's re-quoted optimal cannot be run on this bundle; and POL-RD-01, which measures only the excess between the recorded pickup event and the recorded dropoff event, registers nothing about a trip that ended short of its destination. The rider's grievance - a trip not completed to the point she booked - is therefore documented and unpriced by the arithmetic.

The rider does not ask the tribunal to invent a distance excess, because the trace is unimpaired and states the opposite. gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 3.09 km against a booked optimal_distance_km of 3.2 km, an excess of -0.11 km, or -3.44%, so neither establishment test in POL-RD-01 (greater than 20% of optimal, and greater than 0.8 km absolute) is satisfied and POL-RD-02's recomputation has no deviation to run on. The rider's case on this record is not a POL-RD-02 refund and she does not press one; she asks the tribunal to decide the short-ended trip that is actually recorded.

The threshold facts are not in dispute and the rider brings no corroboration handicap to them. trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-00536 with a consistent pickup window on 2026-09-24 - requested 13:05:00, accepted 13:05:40, first fix 13:11:40 - which satisfies POL-RD-08(a), and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 with deviation_claims_60d_substantiated 0, so the extra-corroboration factor in POL-RD-08 never engages against her and she is not a claim-farming rider whose assertions require strengthening.

The one question this dispute turns on - whether the driver was entitled to end the trip 200 metres short of the booked pin - is carried by no admissible artifact in the bundle. The traffic_advisory is MISSING at weight 0.0 and a missing artifact can carry no fact under POL-GEN-02(3); the chat_log is empty, so neither an instruction to stop short nor the driver's claimed notice to the rider is recorded anywhere; and the GPS arrival facts are unavailable because trip_record.pickup_zone_class is null, so no zone thresholds and no qualifying-run facts were computed. The trace itself is unimpaired (100% coverage, 73 fixes at a 10 second cadence, no gap over 90 seconds), so this is not a POL-RD-07 trace-integrity case - it is a case in which the deciding fact is simply absent from the evidence, so confidence in any finding on it cannot reach the 0.70 platform floor and POL-RD-10(1) requires ESCALATE in place of a final ruling. Under POL-GEN-03 that is the outcome that leaves the rider not carrying the disputed SGD 10.29: an escalated fee is held rather than collected or refunded, and the rider asks that the amount be held pending review of the missing advisory and the unpriced short-ended dropoff.

The platform's own derivation records NO deviation on this trip: the measured excess is -0.11 km against a 0.8 km absolute threshold and -3.4375% against a 20% proportional threshold. Under POL-RD-01 a route deviation is ESTABLISHED only when the excess exceeds 20% of optimal_distance_km AND exceeds 0.8 km; here the driven distance is actually shorter than the booking optimal, so both gates fail by a wide margin. POL-RD-01 is explicit that where either establishment test fails no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement and forbids citing the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km for the threshold test. The governing figure is 3.09 km (derived.deviation.trace_distance_km), set against a booking optimal of 3.2 km. Even on the trip_record's own convenience copy the driven distance is 3.1 km, again below the 3.2 km optimal. There is no positive excess to measure on any reading of the record, so POL-RD-01 cannot be satisfied.

The trace that produced that measurement is unimpaired for policy purposes: 73 fixes at a 10 second cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0.0 seconds. None of the POL-RD-07(a) to (c) limbs is met (no gap over 90 s, no straight-line jump over 500 m, no sustained interval above 30 s), so the trace is a sound and admissible basis for the POL-RD-01 threshold test and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation is engaged.

The rider's own narrative and the dropoff field both describe a SHORTFALL, not an excess: the recorded dropoff is 'Marina Coastal Dr, 210 m short of the pier', matching the rider's account that the driver stopped about 200 m before the pin. POL-RD-01 measures deviation as actual_distance_km minus optimal_distance_km, so a stop short of the pin is by construction incapable of establishing a deviation — it can only reduce the measure, which is exactly what the -0.11 km figure shows.

No pickup or dropoff relocation is on the record: trip_record.dropoff_amended_at and pickup_amended_at are both null, so no amended endpoint and no amended optimal exist under POL-RD-05. The booked 3.2 km optimal stands as the correct comparator, there is no re-quote to re-run the threshold against, and no substitute figure needs to be derived.

The in-app chat export for this trip contains zero messages (message_count 0, empty messages array). There is therefore no recorded rider instruction and no waypoint_hint on which POL-RD-04 could operate, and no rider message by which the dropoff point could have been relocated. Neither the rider-requested-detour clause nor any chat-based route excuse is available on this record to either side, and nothing in the chat undermines the driver.

No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires on this bundle. The trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown (all TRP-00536); the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c); the trip timestamps are consistent (pickup 13:05/13:10, start 13:11:40, end 13:23:40); and no charge line lacks a counterpart in the trace or trip record. The case is therefore fully rulable and must not be diverted to a human reviewer.

The traffic advisory for this trip is MISSING at weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and the driver does not invoke POL-RD-03 or rest on any external traffic cause, so nothing turns on its absence. Under POL-RD-13 an assertion that cites no advisory identifier is not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, so the absent advisory is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it, and it does not trigger POL-RD-10(5).

The fare ledger reconciles line by line: base fare 3.80 + distance 2.33 + time 3.36 + platform fee 0.80 = 10.29 charged, with no ERP gantry charged, no toll and no airport surcharge on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport. There is no phantom line and no wrongly applied surcharge, so no billing-integrity refund is available under POL-RD-09(4), and no pass-through correction is due under POL-RD-09.

The driver's profile discloses no repeat deviation pattern: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 250 completed_trips_90d, a ratio of 0.000 against the 0.05 limb and 0 against the count-of-3 limb. The POL-RD-06 test is not satisfied, so no full-refund uplift and no driver-conduct referral is licensed.

POL-RD-08 puts the initial burden on the rider to show, citing evidence IDs, an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired trace. She has not discharged it: the only trace on file records -0.11 km, and her rider_profile shows deviation_claims_60d of 0, which neither adds a corroboration requirement nor supplies any support for the claim. The burden never shifts to the driver.

Because no deviation is established, POL-RD-01 fixes the outcome at NO_ACTION. NO_ACTION is party-relative under POL-GEN-03: on this rider-filed dispute, where fare_breakdown.payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, it leaves the 10.29 charge standing exactly as it is and returns nothing to the rider. The present payment state — the fare in the driver's hands — is preserved.

Both gates fail — the trip was shorter than optimal, not longer — so no deviation is established and POL-RD-02 never runs. For transparency only: had it run it would have compared a charged_total of 10.29 against a recomputed fare of 9.24, a refund of 1.05; that figure is not payable because there is no deviation to trigger it.

There is no traffic advisory on file for this trip (EV-ADVIS-00536-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), so under POL-RD-13 and POL-RD-08 the assertion carries no weight and reduces no excess, and POL-RD-03 cannot be run to exonerate anything. The chat log is empty, so no rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04 is available either, and no amended endpoint exists for POL-RD-05.

The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes (73 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, no inter-fix gap over 90 seconds), and none of the POL-RD-10 escalation triggers fires — in particular the absent advisory was cited by no party as an exculpatory ground, so POL-RD-13(1) applies and this is not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation. The case is therefore decided on the record, and there is no POL-RD-06 repeat-pattern finding (deviation_flags_90d 0 over 250 completed trips).

Result: NO_ACTION. The SGD 10.29 charged stands exactly as it is; nothing is refunded and nothing is paid to the driver. The rider's grievance — being set down short of her pin and having to run the last stretch with two small children — is real and is recorded on the trip record itself, but the route-deviation policy prices excess distance, not a short stop, and on this record there is no excess to price. POL-RD-01 requires an excess both greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20% of optimal; here the trip is shorter than the booking optimal, so both tests fail and no deviation exists. POL-RD-01 fixes that outcome at NO_ACTION.

Rider, your account matters and it is corroborated: the trip_record dropoff is labelled 'Marina Coastal Dr, 210 m short of the pier' and the driver's own statement concedes the same 200-metre gap. But that is a short-ended trip, not a route deviation, and this policy prices only excess distance. The fare reconciles line by line — base fare 3.80 + distance 2.33 + time 3.36 + platform fee 0.80 = 10.29 charged — with no ERP gantry, no toll and no airport surcharge, so the only deviation-independent refund, POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity, is not available on this record. POL-RD-05 (dropoff relocation) cannot be run either: dropoff_amended_at and pickup_amended_at are both null, so there is no amendment and no amended optimal to re-measure against; that is why the short stop is documented but unpriced by the arithmetic.

Driver, your explanation that the last stretch is a bus lane and you stopped at the nearest legal point is an asserted external traffic cause. There is no traffic advisory on file — EV-ADVIS-00536-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT — so under POL-RD-13 and POL-RD-08 the uncited assertion carries no weight and exonerates nothing. That does not change the result in either direction: you were never charged with a deviation to excuse, and the rider's claim fails on the absence of an excess, not on your excuse. Because you named no advisory identifier, POL-RD-13(1) treats the missing advisory as a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction, and it does not trigger POL-RD-10(5).

I checked every escalation trigger in POL-RD-10: the trip identifiers match (TRP-00536 on trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown), the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c), the timestamps run forward and agree, no exculpatory clause has been invoked with a proper citation against a missing or misfitting artifact, and no charge line is unmatched. No escalation is engaged; the case is rulable.

No repeat-deviation pattern arises — driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 250 completed trips in 90 days — so POL-RD-06 does not fire, there is no full-refund uplift and no driver-conduct referral. There is no billing-integrity finding, so no POL-RD-09(4) referral. No driver compensation arises under POL-RD-04: the rider was billed for 3.1 km against a 3.09 km trace, so there is no unbilled-distance shortfall.

Because no deviation is established, POL-RD-02 never runs; its figures (charged 10.29, recomputed 9.24, difference 1.05) are arithmetic that only applies where a deviation exists, and no distance-or-time refund is due. Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION on this rider-filed dispute leaves fare_breakdown.payment_status and refund_issued_sgd exactly as they are, so the contested SGD 10.29 stands and nothing is refunded. Confidence is 0.90, capped by the weight-1.0 GPS trace and trip record that carry the deciding measurement.
